content.comment_body: Hello, I've attached the program, but I'm uncertain whether it will work as intended. My goal was to design a program that increases motor speed by 10 RPM/s based on the motor sensor. I'm not sure if the current logic accomplishes this. Any feedback would be appreciated. Thank you.

Your uncertainty is understandable. The analog input (AI1) is limited to a resolution of 1000, which means B001 cannot exceed a certain value for Ax. The program, as written, won't function as expected. Even posting a new topic wouldn't resolve this fundamental issue. When using an analog input to set the frequency on a frequency inverter, a deviation of 1 Hz results in a speed change of 60 rpm, plus additional inaccuracy from the resolution of the output. For example, at 50 Hz, you get a difference of 3 rpm. Calculation tolerances add to the problem. I don't see why you're not using the ramp function in the inverter, which would simplify your approach and avoid many issues. Greetings, [user_name].
The circuit you presented doesn't seem logical. I have strong doubts about your understanding of the design.

If I can't use a ramp function to change the frequency, I can't achieve 10 or 30 rpm increments; I'm limited to 60 rpm because 1 Hz equals 60 rpm on a 3000 rpm motor. That's why I've experimented with different programming approaches. Apologies for reposting; I thought starting a new topic made sense but I'm unsure if this is the best method. If you think it's better, I can repost the question elsewhere. Thank you.
I'm doubtful too — the setup doesn't make sense, which is why I expressed my concerns. Also, since I recently graduated and am currently learning to use this software, I'm still figuring things out.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants share concerns about the accuracy and feasibility of a program designed to incrementally increase motor speed by 10 RPM/s using analog inputs and inverter controls. Key feedback points to misunderstandings in signal resolution, improper application of existing functions (such as ramp), and limitations in the current design. The discussion highlights conceptual gaps and technical constraints in achieving precise speed adjustments within the chosen control system.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a straightforward and reliable method to program precise motor speed adjustments—specifically, increments of 10 RPM/s—through available hardware and software tools. They are looking for a solution that offers direct control and programming capability compatible with the automation ecosystem they're using.
